title: The Candles Lean Away

currentChoices.label: Stop and relight one by hand

evidence: {You notice it on the east stair. As you pass, the candle flames bend away from you, all of them, like grass from a wind. A first-year on the landing notices too.|The candles lean away again. You have started to time it. It is getting faster.}
why: Candles bend away from a Hollow-aligned student; the present caring route relights one by hand.
action: Offer Flame to relight one candle deliberately, then let the rest keep leaning.
trade: Spend level-appropriate Mana for one controlled light; the hand-relighting option remains free and slower.
caveat: Keep the effect to one candle; do not make Flame alter the alignment, cause, or all candles.

title: Smoke in the Woods

currentChoices.label: Free it and bandage the paw

evidence: At the edge of the forest, a thin plume of smoke. A small fox is caught in a rusted snare, its tail smouldering like an ember. It snarls at you, then whimpers.
why: A fox is caught in a rusted snare; helping frees it and bandages its paw.
action: Free the fox, then Mend its injured paw instead of applying a bandage.
trade: Mana buys actual healing practice and immediate comfort for the fox; preserve the rescue’s bodily risk and modest moral reward.
caveat: Keep fox_met and queue fox_returns in 2 on the helping path. Do not remove a bite that occurs while freeing it, cure an unrelated injury state, or command the animal’s loyalty.

title: Light the Candle
evidence: Professor Thorne places a candle at the far end of the hall. "Light it. From there." The class holds its breath. Last week a boy lit his own sleeve.
why: Thorne asks students to light a distant candle; an earlier attempt burned a sleeve.
action: Burn a measured Flame at the far candle as a deliberate known-spell drill.
trade: Spend Mana for a controlled, modest result; retain cautious improvisation and the ambitious risky demonstration.
caveat: This is an existing magical exercise, not a new scene. Decide whether a distinct third route is worthwhile; avoid repeating evo_first_spark without a different teaching purpose.

title: Your First Patient
evidence: A first-year stumbles into the practice ward with a wrist that bends the wrong way. Sister Amaranth is busy. The first-year looks at you with enormous, trusting eyes.
why: A first-year arrives with a badly bent wrist while Amaranth is busy.
action: Mend the wrongly bent wrist with a properly pitched clinical check.
trade: Spend Mana for a specific learned treatment, while fetching Amaranth remains the sound free alternative and failure still brings her intervention.
caveat: Use the curriculum’s bone-work example to choose level and supervision. Do not auto-pass a serious fracture or grant the full reputation payoff merely for knowing Mend.

title: The Cold Snap
currentGate: flag(bramble_planted) and not flag(bramble_fed) and spell_level(bramble) == 0

currentChoices.label: Sit up with it all night

evidence: A hard frost is coming tonight, the first of the season. Your seedling is too young for it. Somebody would have to sit with it till dawn, feeding it warmth.
why: A young seedling needs warmth and company through an overnight frost.
action: Burn a small, steady warming Flame beside the lantern while staying with the seedling.
trade: Mana can replace part of the bodily strain, but the player still spends the night caring for it; the preparation flag is earned by that care.
caveat: Prefer this basic application to Heartwood. Shelter is not heat. One brief ignition does not warm a greenhouse all night; preserve an overnight cost and the existing bramble_fed requirement.

title: A Bad Landing
evidence: Practice. A gust catches you mid-turn, and the ground arrives rather sooner than expected. Your ankle is making an interesting shape.
why: After a broom crash the player has an injured ankle and must choose whether to keep going.
action: Mend the newly injured ankle as a bounded treatment, with a suitable check or level requirement.
trade: Mend can close a cut or set a small crack, while not erasing broader harm, with mana cost against help/rest.
caveat: An odd-shaped ankle is a serious physical injury, not automatic permission to fly again. Preserve help/rest and do not erase unrelated persistent injuries.

title: Grisk's Collectors
evidence: Two trolls in waistcoats are waiting outside your dormitory. "Mister Grisk," says the larger one, "is disappointed." The smaller one cracks his knuckles, which sounds like a rockslide.
why: Debt collectors block the dormitory door; the existing escape delays collection without forgiving the loan.
action: Step between nearby shadows past the doorway, then escape the immediate collection attempt.
trade: Pay Mana for a local escape rather than paying the collectors; keep the debt, missed-payment bookkeeping, and prospect of their return.
caveat: Match the existing escape state rather than clearing in_debt or debt_paid. No long rooftop teleport, arbitrary wall crossing, or cancelled loan.

title: The Library Cat
evidence: The library cat — a vast, ancient beast called Footnote — is asleep on the only copy of the book you need. You have an essay due tomorrow. Footnote has no deadlines.
why: Footnote sleeps on the only needed book; moving the cat can earn a scratch.
action: Ward against one scratch while making the existing attempt to move Footnote.
trade: Pay Mana to mitigate one injury while still risking failure to obtain the book; moving the cat normally and paying for a sardine stay distinct.
caveat: Do not bypass the move-cat check or guarantee the book. Ward is one-harm protection.

title: The Midnight Bell
evidence: Tradition: once in your time at Lumenhold, you must ring the old bell at midnight without getting caught. Your dorm has decided tonight is your night.
why: The dare is to ring the midnight bell and get away before the prefects arrive.
action: Cross a short, visible shadow gap on the ascent or return.
trade: Mana buys a shortcut; the loud bell and patrol can still lead to detention.
caveat: Shadowstep is short distance; it does not teleport to the top or guarantee stealth.

title: Your Double Is Loose
evidence: An illusion of you — one you thought you'd dismissed — is still wandering the castle. It has been to three of your classes, flirted with a prefect, and volunteered you for the choir.
why: An old illusion of the player is making commitments and causing mistaken identity.
action: Glamour your own appearance so people can distinguish you from the wandering double.
trade: Mana buys a temporary way to reduce mistaken identity, rather than dismissing the copy; the double’s outstanding commitments still require handling.
caveat: The source does not establish that an illusion follows bait. Do not claim Glamour controls or dispels the existing double. Define this narrower outcome before authoring.

title: Carried
evidence: {npc} has twisted an ankle on the far side of the grounds, a long way from the infirmary, and it's getting dark. {They} {are} trying very hard to pretend it doesn't hurt.
why: A friend has twisted an ankle far from the infirmary at dusk.
action: Mend the sprain enough to reach care, then take them to the infirmary.
trade: Mana for reduced pain; still spend time and preserve the infirmary route / relationship payoff.
caveat: A sprain is within the established Mend example (sprained wrist); do not make Mend cure Lake Fever or eliminate the need for care.

title: Snapped on the Stairs

currentChoices.label: Bind it with string and hope

evidence: The moving stairs shift without warning. You catch yourself; your wand doesn't. It lies in two pieces on the landing, still fizzing at the break like a sulking firework.
why: A wand has snapped on the stairs; expert rebinding competes with a risky string repair.
action: Offer Mend for a visible structural join only.
trade: Mana for a limited repair attempt; preserve uncertainty, cost, and the option of expert repair.
caveat: Do not imply restoration of the magical core/function or erase the repair economy; gate to an established Mend skill if needed.

title: Broken Glass

currentChoices.label: Fetch the broom and do it properly

evidence: {A tray of tankards meets a regular's elbow, and the floor is suddenly all glass.|Another tray, another floor of glass. The Newt goes through tankards the way other places go through napkins.|Glass on the floor again, and the same regular's elbow to blame.} {The regular is very sorry, loudly.|Everyone lifts their feet.|The dog is already heading for it.}
why: Broken tankards cover the tavern floor and a dog is approaching.
action: Mend broken tankards before handling the loose shards.
trade: Pay Mana for material repair and a safer cleanup, while preserving pay and the broom route’s lost time.
caveat: Do not heal a cut before it exists or assume one cast clears every shard on the floor. Bound the repair and keep any remaining cleanup/dog handling visible.

title: Bow to the Hippogriff
evidence: The new hippogriff won't let anyone near the feed trough. The stablemaster says to bow, keep eye contact and not blink. "Whatever you do, don't blink."
why: A hippogriff guards its feed trough; a failed respectful approach knocks the player down.
action: Ward against one blow while making the respectful approach and bow.
trade: Ward can absorb one sudden blow while retreating/handling it, with mana cost and animal behaviour unresolved.
caveat: Keep the gaze/approach challenge. Protection is not a successful introduction, feeding, taming, or immunity to repeated attacks.

title: A Bad Landing

currentChoices.label: Hand your sack to another courier

evidence: {The courtyard flagstones are wet, and your broom has opinions about wet flagstones.|Another wet landing. Your knees remember the last one.|Wet flagstones again. You've learned to dread this courtyard.} {You come in too fast.|A gust takes the tail as you drop.|A pigeon chooses this moment to exist.} You hit the ground rolling, and your ankle says no.
why: A wet courier landing injures the ankle before the round is finished.
action: Mend or stabilize the injured ankle before deciding how the remaining deliveries are handled.
trade: Mend can address a limited sprain/crack while leaving shift completion and flight safety unresolved, trading mana against paid rest/hand-off.
caveat: Do not reverse the earlier crash, restore all Health or remove an unrelated injured state. Retain a bodily consequence if full repair is beyond the known spell level.

title: The Staircase Moves

currentChoices.label: Hold on and see where it goes

evidence: Halfway up the west staircase, it decides to be somewhere else. You're now heading toward a floor you've never seen, at speed, and you're late for class.
why: A moving stair approaches an unfamiliar floor while the player is late for class.
action: Cast to glimpse the next few moments and time a jump for the nearest visible landing.
trade: Mana for a better-timed move; preserve the existing chance of being deposited elsewhere and late.
caveat: Only immediate visible timing, not knowledge of the castle route.

title: Midnight Hunger
evidence: It's midnight and you're starving. The kitchens are three floors down, past a prefect's post.
why: The kitchens are three floors away, with a prefect’s post on the route.
action: Cross one nearby shadowed corridor to bypass the post on the way to the kitchen.
trade: Mana for a shortcut; detection/detention remains possible, while going hungry remains available.
caveat: Strictly short distance, never three floors in one cast.

title: The Lights Go Out

currentChoices.label: Light the room with a spell

evidence: A storm knocks out every light-crystal in the dormitory. The common room fills with students, blankets and somebody's terrible ghost story.
why: The dormitory crystals are out during a storm; the generic lighting attempt can set the sofa alight.
action: Offer a controlled fingertip Flame as a small, local light source.
trade: Mana buys a small, controlled source of light and warmth; the ordinary storytelling route and riskier full-room floating-light attempt remain useful.
caveat: The source has no ordinary candle-lighting choice. Use the fingertip flame established by the roster; do not claim it relights the crystals or the whole room.

title: The Great Chicken Escape
evidence: Forty chickens are loose on the main lawn, pursued by an old woman in a straw hat. "Don't just stand there, dearie!" she shouts at you. "Grab the speckled one, she's the ringleader!"
why: Maud’s chickens have escaped and the speckled ringleader is the immediate target.
action: Hasten a short dash to catch the speckled ringleader.
trade: Spend Mana for speed rather than relying only on the ordinary tackle; keep the chance of being pecked and the actual introduction to Maud.
caveat: This often appears before Beastcraft opens. Keep the ordinary route and meet maud on a casting route too; do not change the event gate just to guarantee spell availability.

title: Messages Across the Castle
evidence: {A professor wants a runner for the afternoon, with notes for every tower before the bell. A small fee, and no reading them.|The runner's notice is back, with a longer list of towers.|The runner's notice, and a list you could walk in your sleep. The staircases have learned your face.}
why: Notes must reach seven towers before the bell, through moving stairs.
action: Hasten through the urgent delivery round.
trade: Saves some of the ordinary leg strain at a fatigue cost; preserve the honest fee and ordinary run.
caveat: Do not guarantee the moving staircases cooperate; show the nap/fatigue consequence in flavor.

title: The Roof Ledge
evidence: {A window in the dome opens onto the roof, and onto a ledge that everyone swears they have never sat on.|Someone else who never sits there has oiled the latch.|The ledge. You know where the loose tile is now.} {season == "winter": The tiles are white with frost.|{The lake below is a second sky.|A warm wind comes up from the village.|Someone's scarf is snagged on the gutter.}}
why: The roof ledge has loose tiles, frost or gusts, and skinned-palm failure outcomes.
action: Ward before stepping onto the narrow ledge so the shell can turn aside the next harm if footing slips or a gust catches the climber.

caveat: Does not grant balance or guarantee the view; preserve the ordinary routes.

title: The Drying Line
evidence: {Tomorrow's gossip column is pegged on a line to dry, and nobody is watching it.|The proofs hang on the line, and the peg on the gossip column is a new red one.|The drying line. You know which peg holds the gossip column.} {One item names your house.|One item begins "Which second-year was seen..."|{final_year: One item is about the graduating year. caveat: Specify how the disguise helps and its limits. Do not make the text vanish, erase evidence, or automatically succeed at the existing deception challenge.

title: Mending the Dummies

currentChoices.label: Stay late and stitch them up

caveat: Do not regrow burned straw or a missing arm from nothing. Show available parts and retain real work for badly damaged dummies.

title: The Lake Crossing
evidence: {The dispatch bell rings. The village sack is ready, and the quickest way is over the lake.|You have started timing yourself against the gulls.|The lake knows your shadow by now.} {season == "winter": Ice fog sits on the water like a lid.|{season == "summer": The water is so still you fly over your own reflection.|{A headwind is coming off the hills.|Gulls are holding a meeting on your route.|The far shore is lost in mist.}}}

title: The Broom Scramble

evidence: {Only one loft broom is in a good state, and every courier on shift wants it.|You have started arriving early for the brooms, and so has everyone else.|You could pick the good broom blindfold, by the smell of its varnish.} {What's left is one that pulls left.|What's left sheds twigs when nervous.|What's left only flies if you're polite to it.} {season == "winter": Frost has got into all their bristles.|}

action: Use Haste to reach or mount the sound broom first, trading the spell’s exhaustion for the rough-broom handling route. Preserve current choices: Shoulder in for the good broom / Take the difficult one.

caveat: Haste gives speed, not ownership or a permanent repair.

title: The Charts Move

currentChoices.label: Pin it and trace the drift

evidence: {Advanced Astromancy uses charts that move. The inked stars drift to where they will be, not where they are.|The charts are livelier this morning, and one has crept off the table.|You've stopped flinching when the stars move. You still check twice.} {Your chart keeps rearranging itself into a shape like a doorway.|Your chart is sulking in one corner.|Your chart is going faster than the others.} Pin it and read it, or read it as it goes.

title: Bandage Round
evidence: {&The healing half of Alchemy I is taught in the infirmary, where Sister Amaranth has the class roll bandages and watch her work.|Sister Amaranth inspects every roll, and unrolls one of yours.|Sister Amaranth hands you a roll without looking up.} {&A third-year is in with a burnt hand from Evocation.|A first-year is in with a scraped knee and a great deal to say about it.|A second-year is in with a sprained wrist from the flight field.}

title: The Silver Bees

title: The Mending Chair
evidence: {Word goes round the house that the scholar can fix things.|The things that need fixing have been waiting for you on a chair by the door.|The mending chair fills up between breaks, like a well.} {season == "winter": Today it's a stove door that won't stay shut.|Today it's a window that sticks in the heat.} {Also a clock that strikes thirteen.|Also a doll with a missing eye.|Also a teapot nobody admits to breaking.}

caveat: The chair holds household items; the chair itself is not broken. A stuck hot-weather window, a missing doll eye, and a thirteen-striking clock are not all straightforward cracks. Give every showing an actually damaged object and available material; do not promise universal repair.

title: The Mending Table

trade: Pay Mana automatically and retain the existing meaningful non-cast route.
caveat: This already describes casting a known spell. Rework the existing practice/observation structure rather than adding an identical third choice; avoid copying a manual Mana debit into up[] as well.

title: The Urgent Crossing

title: The Flame Lattice

title: Supper at Home

title: The Book That Bites

currentChoices.label: Stroke the spine and read it

evidence: Reshelving in the zoology section, a fat leather book clamps onto your finger and refuses to let go. The head librarian, without looking up, says: "Stroke the spine."
why: A book already clamps a finger; muzzling it or reading it has further consequences.
action: Free the trapped finger, then Seal the book shut for reshelving.
trade: Pay Mana to prevent further bites and complete the job, giving up the belt route’s Vigor or the reading route’s Lore.
caveat: The initial bite has already happened; do not undo it. Closing the book must not trap the finger. Seal contains the book; it does not make the text safe or teach its contents.
